title: The Fifth Voyage of Sindbad
full_text:
Sindbad began his fifth narrative:

'On my fifth voyage, our crew landed on a deserted island and discovered another gigantic egg of the Rukh. Despite my warnings, the foolish sailors broke the shell with axes to roast the young chick.

Suddenly, the two parent birds returned, darkening the sky! Each bird held a colossal boulder in its talons, large as a house. Circling above our ship, they dropped the boulders: one struck the sea, raising a tidal wave, and the second smashed our vessel to splinters!

I clung to a plank and was washed ashore on an enchanted island filled with blooming fruit trees and crystal streams.

Beside a brook sat an old man clothed in leaves, who seemed feeble and signaled that he wished to be carried across the stream. Moved by pity, I lifted him onto my shoulders and carried him across the water.

But the moment we reached the other side, the old man clamped his sinewy legs around my neck with an iron grip! He was the dreadful Old Man of the Sea! For weeks, he rode my back day and night, kicking my ribs, sleeping with his legs locked around my throat, forcing me to gather fruit for his meals while I groaned under the tyrannical burden.

One afternoon, I hollowed out a large gourd, pressed the juice of wild grapes into it, and left it in the sun until it fermented into fragrant wine.

I drank and began to sing. The tyrant took the gourd, drank greedily, and became intoxicated. His iron grip relaxed, and he tumbled limp onto the grass.

I cast off the burden, leaped to my feet, and ran to the shore, where a passing ship rescued me. The sailors marveled: 'None has ever escaped from the Old Man of the Sea save you!' I returned home in peace, having broken the heaviest yoke through presence of mind.'
moral: Beware of taking tyrannical burdens upon your shoulders; wit and temperance liberate the oppressed.
